Vector Set Across Day Files Example

One vector index per day, searched as one through a .vixset manifest: day ranges, archived days and a live writer.

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Source

What It Shows

A gxVectorSet (gxvset.h) searches many .vix files as one. The files are listed in a small text manifest, <name>.vixset, next to them:

  1. Five day files in YYYY/MM/DD folders, 500 vectors each, tag 2 = the day. AddFile() lists each one with its node counts, the range of its tag 2 and a CRC of its header; the manifest is printed.
  2. One search across the days with 1 and with 4 threads: every result names its file, and the results are the same for any thread count.
  3. A day range: the files whose tag 2 range is outside it are skipped from the manifest alone, without being opened.
  4. A day archived (its file moved away): the set skips it and counts it as missing; with strict set the search is an error instead.
  5. The live day: its writer keeps its own index open and puts it in the set with AttachOpen(), so searches see its newest vectors at once; Refresh() writes the new counts and range into the manifest.

Running It

vector_days [WORK_FOLDER]

Exit code 0 when every check passes.

Source

examples/oodb/vector_days.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as vector_days and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
